blocks.title: Reverse engineer shipped software with evidence
blocks.description: REA gives the agent a structured toolset for investigating compiled or packaged applications. Every claim is backed by an Evidence record that lists the files, offsets, hashes, and limitations behind it.

items.title: Native & firmware analysis
items.description: Disassemble compiled binaries and firmware with bundled REA tools and optional Ghidra. Compare versions, explain features, and surface unsigned code without leaving the conversation.

items.title: JavaScript & Electron apps
items.description: Map shipped ASAR archives, ESM modules and the IPC surface of Electron apps back to their source. Read the build steps that produced the artifact you are debugging.

items.title: Managed code (.NET / JVM)
items.description: Decompile managed assemblies and bytecode into something readable. Recover symbols, infer call graphs, and explain behaviour even when the source repository is gone.

items.title: Runtime observation
items.description: Capture live traffic, logs and process state with REA's runtime providers (Fiddler, mitmproxy-style hooks, launched-app observation) so the agent can answer questions about a running program.

showcase.user_prompt: Closed-source Electron app at /tmp/sample.app: what did 2.3 add over 2.2, and which IPC channels are new?
showcase.assistant_reply: REA diffed IPC across both ASAR archives: 2.3 adds sync/v2, telemetry/v2.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: Add the official REA plugin from the Astravia marketplace. The plugin ships the bundled Skill so the agent knows when to call REA.

items.title: Install the REA CLI
items.description: Astravia probes `npx -y rea-agents@latest --version` on first use. The CLI caches the package locally; no global install is performed.

items.title: Connect the engine you need
items.description: Native and firmware work reads best with Ghidra installed locally; JavaScript and Electron work needs no extra engine. The doctor command reports which provider is missing.

items.title: Ask the agent
items.description: Point the agent at a file, package, or running app and ask a question. REA returns an Evidence record that the agent surfaces in chat.

blocks.content: The agent never installs anything on your machine on its own. The plugin's tool panel runs a real version probe, and marks a tool ready only when that holds up. Hopper can be installed through REA's own channel; tools that Homebrew carries (apktool, binwalk, rizin, adb) are installed only after you press the button. Node.js, Ghidra, IDA and JADX still have to come from you — they need environment variables or a licence, so installing them alone does not make them ready.
Reverse engineering can be subject to local law and license terms. Confirm you have the right to analyze a given artifact before invoking REA on it.
